items.title: Seized scam centre in Myanmar offers rare glimpse into industry targeting Australians
items.description: The scam industry in Myanmar is morphing and heading into the jungle rather than disappearing since a crackdown began.

items.title: Sixteen-year-old in custody suspected of killing mother, injuring little sister
items.description: Police say a teenage boy is suspected to have stabbed his mother to death and seriously injured his 12-year-old sister in an alleged family violence homicide in Perth's south-east.

items.title: Who paid for Pauline Hanson's trip to Europe? Not taxpayers, she says
items.description: In her first appearance since returning to Australia, Pauline Hanson fields questions about her trip to Europe with billionaire Gina Rinehart.

items.title: Job system broken for workers, booming for private equity, report says
items.description: A new report argues Australia's employment services system is failing jobseekers, while filling the pockets of private equity firms and millionaires.

items.title: Kumanjayi Little Baby child protection review finds departmental failings
items.description: Nearly three months since the death of Kumanjayi Little Baby, an interim report into her family circumstances prior to the tragedy has been handed down.

items.title: AI companies 'stole' Australian culture, news bosses say as they call for licensing deals
items.description: The heads of the ABC, SBS, Nine and News Corp say AI companies should strike licensing deals rather than freely train on Australian news, warning journalism is a public good that must be protected.

items.title: Police confirm investigation involving incident with NT administrator
items.description: Former army commando turned Labor MP, Luke Gosling, has denied involvement in an alleged incident with King Charles's representative in the NT.

items.title: Former Catholic bishop sexually abused boys at 'shirts-off' parties, court hears
items.description: One of Australia's longest serving senior Catholic clerics had a sexual interest in young Aboriginal men and abused them in Western Australia's far north over several years, a Perth court hears.

items.title: Armed with axes and a machete, ICE protester 'attacked' US federal building, FBI says
items.description: A former US Army soldier protesting Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has been arrested in New York after allegedly setting off fireworks, lighting a fire and shooting a pellet gun outside a federal office building.

items.title: Indonesia sentences leader of baby-trafficking ring to seven years' jail
items.description: Lie Siu Luan, 70, was the leader of a group of 19 people accused of trafficking babies in Indonesia and Singapore.

items.title: What's behind the protests in New Delhi?
items.description: Thousands of protesters under the banner of the Cockroach Janta Party have marched on India's parliament and clashed with the authorities. Here's why.

items.title: Mother of identical quadruplets calls them her 'miracle babies'
items.description: A maternal foetal medicine expert believes identical quadruplets born in Brisbane may be even rarer than one in 15 million, given they shared a placenta.

items.title: Officer handcuffed teen in lead-up to police station rape, court told
items.description: A NSW Police officer locked a 17-year-old in a cell and handcuffed her on separate occasions before he sexually assaulted her in a police station in 1998, a court has heard.

items.title: Inquest to determine whether man killed his mother and staged her death
items.description: An inquest is investigating whether a man killed his mother before placing her in the driver's seat of her car to stage that she was behind the wheel during a crash.

items.title: Kids do feel the cold. So why won't they wear a jumper?
items.description: Do kids really not feel the cold like adults do? Or are they just expressing their independence? And when should you insist?

items.title: Ian doesn't want children. He's part of a growing trend among men
items.description: About 15 per cent of Australian men say they don't want children, an increase from 11 per cent in 2005. Ian says his own childhood played a large part in his decision.

items.title: Why 'narcissist' bosses are more likely to oppose work from home
items.description: Research published last month found narcissistic leaders — those with a tendency to be self-centred and entitled — were more likely than others to resist remote work. Why? The study concluded "it interferes with their motivations for power and status".

items.title: India steps up response to US, Iran deadly ship strikes
items.description: The Indian government is taking action after 10 sailors were killed and dozens more injured in attacks on commercial cargo ships and oil tankers during the battle for control of the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Philippines, China clash in South China Sea
items.description: Vision posted online by the Philippines Coast Guard shows Filipino and Chinese personnel briefly engaging each other from inflatable boats, with the Philippines accusing China of assaulting one of its navy staff.

items.title: Stubborn stigma fuelling shocking violence against sex workers in Australia
items.description: A new inquiry into violence against sex workers in Australia and Thailand comes just weeks after the murder of Thai teenager Tunchanok Donhomla, allegedly by an Australian man.

items.title: Tony Modra shares post-surgery photos after truck crash
items.description: AFL legend Tony Modra shares a post-crash update on social media, posting photos of him in hospital and with family, and saying he is now "getting out and about".

items.title: Synagogue had requests for security funding rejected before firebombing
items.description: Jewish leaders have given evidence to the Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion regarding security concerns for synagogues nationwide.

items.title: Australian EV owners deal with 'range anxiety'. China has almost eliminated it
items.description: You can swap an empty electric vehicle battery in about four minutes in China. It is part of how China has come to dominate the EV industry.

items.title: Police probe use of force on handcuffed teen injured during Perth arrest
items.description: A handcuffed teenager was injured when he was forced to the ground by a police officer, sparking a WA Police review after video of the incident emerged.

items.title: Two dead after house fire south of Brisbane
items.description: An investigation is underway into the cause of a house fire south of Brisbane.
